What Is Revenue Intelligence?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 17 November 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

Revenue intelligence is software that captures what sellers and buyers actually do, such as emails, meetings and calls, joins it to CRM data and uses it to score deals, flag risks and support the forecast. It tests whether a deal is as healthy as the seller says. Gartner now files it within a wider market, revenue action orchestration, which adds AI assistants and agents that act on the signals.

What revenue intelligence means

A CRM records what sellers type in. Revenue intelligence adds what happened: emails, meetings, attendees and, through conversation intelligence, what was said on calls. It compares that activity with the CRM's stage, amount and close date. A deal in negotiation with no buyer reply for three weeks is a risk the CRM alone does not show.

Salesforce's Trailhead material shows the typical parts: Revenue Insights dashboards, Pipeline Inspection, which "gives sellers a consolidated view of opportunities and pipeline metrics", and Salesforce Forecasting. Underneath sit Einstein Activity Capture, which syncs email and calendar data, deal health predictions and Opportunity Scoring from 1 to 99.

Gong's deal boards "integrate with your CRM while adding AI insights", show a timeline of calls and emails, and let users update CRM fields from the board.

ComponentWhat it doesTypical inputs
Activity captureLogs emails, meetings and calls against accounts and dealsEmail, calendar, dialler, video platforms
Deal scoringRates each deal's health or likelihood to closeActivity, CRM fields, past outcomes
Risk warningsFlags patterns such as silence or one engaged contactActivity and stage history
Pipeline inspectionShows changes in amount, stage and close date over timeCRM history snapshots
ForecastingRolls deals into a forecast, with AI predictions beside seller callsForecast categories, scores, history

Where the category sits now

Gartner has redrawn the category lines. Its Magic Quadrant for revenue action orchestration, dated 15 December 2025, was the first for that market. Gartner's market page describes it as "a category of technology vendors that use AI to improve sales productivity" and says it "serves as the primary system of seller action and a single source of truth for sales interactions".

Gartner lists seven mandatory features: deal scoring and pipeline analytics, sales skills coaching, an AI sales assistant, data interoperability including Model Context Protocol support, advanced activity intelligence, AI-guided actions that can dispatch agents, and programmable action orchestration with governance controls. A vendor press release describes the category as uniting sales engagement, revenue intelligence and sales force automation; that is the vendors' summary. For a buyer, a "revenue intelligence" shortlist now spans products that only observe and products that also act.

Why it matters for a commercial team

The main use is deal and forecast review. A manager can see whether the buyer has replied, who attended meetings and how the close date has moved. How to combine these signals with seller calls is set out in Forecasting That Holds.

In lowob's model, revenue intelligence spans the wiring and the reasoning layer: it reads the store and produces signals. Three cautions follow. A deal score is a prediction, so score it against what closed, like any forecast call. Acting on a signal moves up the autonomy dial. A warning is level 0 and a drafted follow-up level 1; an agent emailing the buyer waits, under Gateway 1, for a person to approve. And a score drop says a deal weakened, not what the team decided to do; that decision belongs in the decision record.

How to evaluate it

CriterionQuestion to ask
Capture coverageWhich email, calendar, call and meeting sources does it read, and for which users?
Data handlingWhere are captured emails and recordings stored, and who sees them?
Score transparencyCan a manager see which signals moved a deal's score?
Back-testingCan past scores be compared with what actually closed?
CRM write-backDo updates land in the CRM with the person who confirmed them?
Action controlsWhich actions can agents take, at what autonomy level, with what approval?
InteroperabilityCan other assistants read its data, for example through MCP?

Start with one meeting: the weekly pipeline review for late-stage deals. Run it from the tool for a quarter and compare its risk flags with the deals that slipped.

lowob takeaways

  • It shows what happened, not what was typed. Activity data tests the seller's view of each deal.
  • Score the scores. A deal score is a prediction and should be checked against outcomes.
  • Watch the line from flag to action. Agents that act on signals move up the autonomy dial and need approval.
  • Reasons still need a record. A falling score is a fact; the response to it is a decision.
